title: Marketing plan (editable template)
audience: Owners and office staff who decide where new and repeat work comes from
learningOutcomes: Choose three marketing channels and state the reason, cost basis and owner for each
Plan at least three months of activities with a channel, an owner and a done date for each
Define three measures with a formula, a data source and a baseline before the plan starts

instruction.heading: What a marketing plan is for
instruction.body: A marketing plan decides where the next customers will come from, how much will be spent to reach them, and how the business will know whether it worked. It is not a list of everything that could be posted. Most home-service businesses grow from a small number of sources: repeat work, referrals, a listing that people search for, and direct contact with people who have agreed to hear from them. The plan should choose three channels and explain why. Choosing more spreads the budget too thin to judge any one of them.

instruction.heading: Defining customers and choosing channels
instruction.body: Start from the target customer table in the business plan. For each segment, write what the customer needs, where they look for a provider and why they would pick this business over another. Then choose three channels that reach those people. For each channel, state the reason, the cost basis (a fee, staff time or materials) and the person responsible. Direct contact should only go to people who have agreed to receive it. An existing relationship does not, on its own, allow marketing messages; inferred consent can apply only in narrow cases, such as an ongoing relationship with marketing tied to it. A business email address published online does not by itself allow marketing. Record the basis for each contact. Electronic messaging and privacy rules apply to outreach.

instruction.heading: Budget, monthly activities and measures
instruction.body: Set a monthly budget and split it across the three channels, keeping a small part for follow-up. Plan activities by month, with one channel, one owner and one done date for each. Define three measures before you start. Repeat customers are counted as a share of jobs in a period. Acquisition cost for a channel is the money spent on it divided by the number of new customers it brought, measured over the same period. Referrals are counted as the number of new customers who name a source. Record a baseline before the plan begins so that any later change is visible rather than remembered.

procedure: List the target customer segments, their needs, and where they look for providers.
Choose three channels and write the reason for each.
For each channel, record the cost basis and the owner.
Record the basis on which each outreach activity may contact people, and leave out any requirement not yet checked.
Set the monthly budget and split it across the three channels.
Plan at least three months of activities, with a channel, an owner and a done date for each.
Define the three measures with a formula, a data source and a baseline figure.
Set the first review date for the end of month one and the second for the end of month three.
Save the template with the date and version number.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaning business with one employee has steady repeat clients but few new enquiries each month. Two of the three channels it used last year brought almost nothing.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which measure would show whether the business should drop a channel, and what should the plan record before dropping it?
workedExamples.reasoning: Acquisition cost by channel shows whether money spent on a channel is bringing customers at a sensible cost, but only if each enquiry is tagged with its source. The plan should first record a baseline: enquiries by source, customers won by source, and spend by source over a set period. Dropping a channel without that record is a guess. The decision rule should say what result would keep, change or drop the channel, and when the decision will be made. This example uses no cost figures; the business enters its own.

equipmentAndPpe: Target customer table from the business plan
Dated record of past enquiries and their source, if kept
Monthly budget figure the business can commit
PPE: not applicable to this lesson

commonErrors.error: Choosing channels because they are popular rather than because the target customers use them.
commonErrors.prevention: Write where each customer segment looks for a provider before choosing any channel.

commonErrors.error: Setting a budget with no owner or done date for each activity.
commonErrors.prevention: Each activity has one owner and one done date.

commonErrors.error: Counting enquiries but not customers won or repeat jobs.
commonErrors.prevention: Count enquiries, quotes, wins and repeat jobs separately, using the same source tags.

commonErrors.error: Contacting people who have not agreed to hear from the business.
commonErrors.prevention: Only contact people on a basis you can record, and check current rules before any campaign.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electronic messaging, privacy and consent rules apply to marketing contact. Do not send unsolicited messages under this plan until current federal requirements have been checked.

Keep advertising claims about results, safety or qualifications accurate and supportable, and do not claim a certification or licence the business does not hold. The ACCC's guidance on false or misleading claims says a business must be able to prove any claim it advertises.

qualityStandard: Three channels are chosen, each with a reason, a cost basis and an owner
Monthly activities cover at least three months and each links to a channel
Each measure has a formula, a data source and a baseline
Each outreach activity states its basis for contact
documentationEvidence: Completed marketing plan template, dated and versioned
Baseline record of enquiries, wins and spend by source
Review notes from the first and third months
summary: Choose three channels and say why each one reaches the target customers.
Every activity needs one owner and one done date.
Measure customers won and cost per new customer, not only enquiries.
Check the rules before contacting anyone.

editableTemplates.title: Marketing plan
editableTemplates.purpose: Sets the target customers, three channels, the budget, monthly activities, the measures and a decision rule for keeping or dropping a channel.

fields.label: Target customer segments
fields.prompt: One row per segment. Columns: segment, what they need, where they look for a provider, why they would choose this business.
fields.guidance: Each segment is specific enough to choose a channel for it.

fields.label: Three marketing channels
fields.prompt: Exactly three rows. Columns: channel, reason for choosing it, cost basis, owner.
fields.guidance: Cost basis is a fee, staff time or materials, using the business's own figures.

fields.label: Monthly marketing budget
fields.prompt: Enter the total you will commit each month.
fields.guidance: Matches the total of the budget split below.

fields.label: Budget split by channel
fields.prompt: Rows: channel 1, channel 2, channel 3, follow-up reserve. Columns: amount per month, share of budget.
fields.guidance: Rows add up to the monthly budget.

fields.label: Activities by month
fields.prompt: Columns: month, activity, channel, owner, done date. Cover at least three months.
fields.guidance: Each activity has one channel, one owner and one done date.

fields.label: Contact basis for outreach
fields.prompt: For each outreach activity, state the basis on which the business may contact the person, and where that basis is recorded. Note any requirement still to be checked.
fields.guidance: Every outreach activity has a stated basis, or is marked as not to be run until confirmed.

fields.label: Measure: repeat customers
fields.prompt: Write the formula, the data source and the baseline figure.
fields.guidance: Formula is repeat jobs as a share of all jobs in the same period.

fields.label: Measure: acquisition cost
fields.prompt: Write the formula, the data source and the baseline, by channel.
fields.guidance: Formula is money spent on a channel divided by new customers it brought, over the same period.

fields.label: Measure: referrals
fields.prompt: Write how referral sources are recorded and the baseline number.
fields.guidance: Every new customer is asked for a source and the answer is recorded.

fields.label: First review date
fields.prompt: Enter the date of the review at the end of month one.
fields.guidance: A date that falls at the end of the first month of the plan.

fields.label: Third-month review date
fields.prompt: Enter the date of the review at the end of month three.
fields.guidance: A date that falls at the end of the third month of the plan.

fields.label: Decision rule for keeping, changing or dropping a channel
fields.prompt: State the result that would cause you to keep, change or drop each channel, and the date you will decide.
fields.guidance: The rule is set before the results come in and refers to the measures above.

levels.meets: Each channel is justified by where a named customer segment looks for a provider.
levels.does_not_meet: Channels are chosen without reference to the customer segments.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Exactly three channels with cost basis and owner

levels.meets: Three channels are listed, each with a reason, a cost basis and a named owner.
levels.does_not_meet: Fewer or more than three channels are listed, or a channel has no owner or cost basis.

levels.meets: The budget split adds up to the monthly budget, and every activity sits under one of the channels with a done date.
levels.does_not_meet: The split does not match the budget, or activities have no channel, owner or date.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Measures are defined with a baseline

levels.meets: Each measure has a formula, a data source and a recorded baseline.
levels.does_not_meet: A measure is named without a formula, a source or a baseline.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Outreach has a stated contact basis

levels.meets: Each outreach activity states the basis for contact, or is marked not to run until confirmed.
levels.does_not_meet: Outreach is planned with no stated basis for contacting people.
